When to use: Use the Button to trigger an action in the current context: submit a form, save, open a dialog, start a process, delete. The filled style is the primary action, and there is only one per view or dialog; stroke is the secondary action, lighter and ghost are supporting actions. destructive is reserved for actions that delete or cannot be undone.

When the element takes the user to another page, use a link, not a button. For more than two or three secondary actions, group them in a Dropdown opened by one button. For an on / off setting that applies immediately, use a switch, which this library does not have yet.
Layout: One primary per view
A single filled button per view or dialog. Every other action is stroke, lighter or ghost.
Order

In a dialog or a form footer, the primary button sits on the right with Cancel just to its left, right-aligned. In a full-page form, the primary button is left-aligned under the fields, with the secondary button to its right. Never mix the two orders in one context.
Destructive apart
A destructive action is separated from the primary one: on the left of the footer, or behind a confirmation dialog whose confirm button is destructive.
Sizes
md by default in forms, sm in dense tables and toolbars, xs only in very dense interfaces. On mobile, dialog buttons stack full width with the primary on top.
Icons

One icon per button, before the label. An icon after the label only for direction or disclosure (next, open a menu). An icon-only button needs an accessible name and a tooltip, and is reserved for universally understood actions.

Do and don’t.do: Start labels with a specific verb
Do and don’t.doText: Users know exactly what happens before they click.
Do and don’t.dontText: “Yes”, “No” or “OK” force users to reread the question and cause errors.

Do and don’t.do: Use one primary button per view
Do and don’t.doText: A single filled button makes the main action obvious.
Do and don’t.dontText: Several filled buttons compete and none reads as the main action.

Do and don’t.do: Write short labels in sentence case
Do and don’t.doText: Sentence case is the easiest to read, and a short label never wraps.
Do and don’t.dontText: All caps slows reading, and a long label wraps or gets cut.

Do and don’t.doText: Distance and a clear name prevent accidental data loss.
Do and don’t.dontText: An adjacent destructive button is easy to hit by mistake.

notes: Contrast
Label on brand filled 4.6:1 in Boreal Light, 4.6:1 in Dark; label on destructive filled 4.8:1; stroke border 6.0:1.
Text must reach 4.5:1, borders and icons 3:1.
Everything passes.
No neutral type
There is no grey secondary button.
The library keeps the palette small.
Use brand stroke, or static-black stroke on a light background.
Icon stroke
Icons use a 1.5 px stroke, hard-coded.
No variable holds an icon stroke width.
Create an icon stroke variable (1.5 next to a medium label, 1.2 next to a regular one).
Static types
static-black and static-white keep the same colours in Light and Dark.
They sit on images or brand colours, not on the page background.
Check the contrast on the actual image or colour behind them.

When to use: Use the Checkbox when the user can select several options in a list, or to turn a single standalone option on or off, such as accepting the terms or receiving a newsletter. Each box is independent: ticking one never changes the others. The indeterminate state is only for a parent box whose children are partly selected, such as a “Select all” row.

When exactly one option must be chosen, use the Radio button for 2 to 7 options, or the Select beyond. A setting that applies immediately, without a form to submit, calls for a switch, which this library does not have yet.
Layout: Vertical by default
One option per line: the list is easy to scan, each box sits next to its own label and a description fits under each option.
Horizontal for 2 or 3 short options
Only when the labels are one or two words and the whole group stays on one line.
Select all
A parent box above the list checks or unchecks every option. It shows the indeterminate dash while only some options are checked.

Do and don’t.doText: A vertical list is faster to scan and clearly pairs each box with its label.
Do and don’t.dont: Use checkboxes for a single choice
Do and don’t.dontText: Users can tick several options when only one is valid. Use the Radio button instead.

Do and don’t.doText: Positive phrasing makes the checked state unambiguous.
Do and don’t.dontText: With a negative label, users cannot tell whether checking means yes or no.

Do and don’t.doText: An explicit “none” option shows that the user answered rather than skipped the question.
Do and don’t.dontText: Several boxes on one line make it unclear which box belongs to which label.

notes: 10 px icon
The check mark and the dash are 10 px, without a variable.
The size scale starts at 12 px.
Add size/5xs (10 px) to 3c. semantic.layout, or keep the fixed value.
Contrast
Empty box border 4.7:1, checked box 4.6:1 in Boreal (3.8 to 5.5:1 in Sylva). Read-only: black check mark on light grey, easily readable. Disabled is exempt.
A box must reach 3:1.
Everything passes.
Accessibility
The box and the label form a single clickable area.
A 16 px box alone is too small to hit.

In code: input type="checkbox" linked to its label; indeterminate set by script; read-only via aria-readonly or a disabled input whose label stays readable; an aria-label when there is no visible label.
Options 4 to 10
The group holds 10 options. Options 4 to 10 are hidden layers, not properties.
Keeps the property panel short.
Show them from the Layers panel when a list needs more than 3 options.
No error state
The checkbox and the group have no error status.
The form keeps the submit button disabled until every required choice is made, so an empty group never has to show an error.
Mark required questions in the group label and keep forms short.

When to use: Use the Dropdown for a list of actions or commands opened from a Button or an icon button: more actions, account menu, sort by, bulk actions. Use the Select as a form field when the user picks one value among 6 to 15 options and the value is submitted with the form.

For 2 to 5 options in a form, use the Radio button, which shows every option at once; for several simultaneous choices, the Checkbox. For a value the user types faster than they find it (a year, a quantity), use the Input. For site navigation, use plain links, not a menu.
Layout: Opens below the trigger
The panel opens under the button or the field, left-aligned with it, and flips up or right when there is no room. It is at least as wide as the trigger, 320 px at most.
Order and groups
The most frequent actions first, related items grouped under a section label or between dividers, and the destructive item last, after a divider.
7 to 10 items
Beyond, the list scrolls and a search row sits at the top. The user header only belongs in an account menu; the footer holds secondary links.
Select anatomy
Same anatomy as the Input: Label above, field, Hint under it. The field is as wide as the expected value, and the options follow a natural order (sizes, months) or the alphabet.

Do and don’t.doText: A divider and the red colour keep an irreversible action away from the frequent ones.
Do and don’t.dont: Mix destructive items with the others
Do and don’t.dontText: A delete item between frequent actions gets hit by mistake.

Do and don’t.do: Use radio buttons for a few options
Do and don’t.doText: Visible options are compared and picked in one click.
Do and don’t.dontText: A select for 2 to 4 options adds clicks and hides the choices.

Do and don’t.do: Keep a visible label on the select
Do and don’t.doText: The label stays after the choice, so users can check their answer.
Do and don’t.dont: Use the placeholder as the label
Do and don’t.dontText: Once a value is chosen, nothing says what the field was.

notes: Contrast
Label 19.8:1, description and shortcut 7.8:1, destructive label 4.8:1 (4.4:1 on the red hover background), check mark 6.0:1, field border 4.7:1.
Text must reach 4.5:1, icons and borders 3:1.
Everything passes. The panel outline (1.3:1) is decorative: the shadow does the separation.
Select panel
Open, the panel is placed in absolute position 68 px under the top of the component, so it covers the Hint as on screen.
An element in the flow would push the Hint down and distort the height of the field.
If the Label is hidden, move the panel up by 24 px by hand.
Switch
No item with a switch: the library has no Switch component yet.
No component is created outside the agreed list.
Add it to _Dropdown item when the Switch exists.
Multiple choice
The Select holds one value. Multiple choice happens in the panel with checkbox items, without tags in the field.
A version with tags needs a field that grows, to design separately.
Plan it when a screen needs it.
Swapped icon
An icon changed through the icon property can lose its colour and stroke.
Figma does not always carry overrides onto a swapped instance.
Reapply the label colour, stroke 1.2 (regular) or 1.5 (medium).

When to use: Use the Radio button when the user must pick exactly one option among a small set of visible choices, from 2 to 7. Showing every option at once helps to compare them, and preselecting a safe default means the group always carries a value.
For several choices at once, or a single standalone option, use the Checkbox. For more than 7 options, or when the screen has no room for the whole list, use the Select.
Layout: Vertical by default
One option per line: the list is easy to scan, the labels align and a description fits under each option.
Horizontal for 2 or 3 short options
Only when the labels are one or two words and the whole group stays on one line.

Do and don’t.doText: When one option is the usual or safest choice, select it by default so the group always has a value.
Do and don’t.dont: Use a single radio button on its own
Do and don’t.dontText: One radio button alone cannot be unselected. For a single standalone option, use a Checkbox.

Do and don’t.do: State the question in the group label
Do and don’t.doText: Short, parallel labels that complete the group label: the user reads the question once.
Do and don’t.dont: Put long labels on a horizontal group
Do and don’t.dontText: Long labels wrap and the options read like a paragraph. Go vertical.

Do and don’t.doText: From 4 options, use the vertical orientation: every label starts on the same line and the list stays easy to scan.
Do and don’t.dontText: Beyond 7 options the list gets long to scan and to compare. Use a Select.

notes: 6 px dot
The centre dot is 6 px, without a variable.
The size scale starts at 12 px.
Add a 6 px size to 3c. semantic.layout, or keep the fixed value.
Contrast
Empty circle border 4.7:1, checked circle 4.6:1 in Boreal (3.8 to 5.5:1 in Sylva). Disabled is exempt.
A circle must reach 3:1.
Everything passes.
Accessibility
The circle and the label form a single clickable area.
A 16 px circle alone is too small to hit.

In code: input type="radio" sharing the same name, linked to its label; group in a fieldset with a legend; arrow keys move between options; read-only via aria-readonly or a disabled input whose label stays readable.
Options 4 to 10
The group holds 10 options. Options 4 to 10 are hidden layers, not properties.
Keeps the property panel short.
Show them from the Layers panel when a list needs more than 3 options.
No error state
The radio button and the group have no error status.
The form keeps the submit button disabled until every required choice is made, so an empty group never has to show an error.
Mark required questions in the group label and keep forms short.

When to use: Use the Input for short, single-line data the user knows and can type: a name, an email address, a phone number, a website, an amount, a search query, a password, or a link to copy. The type sets the right structure and keyboard: a country code for phone, an https:// prefix for website, a currency for amount, a magnifier and a shortcut for search, a show / hide button for password, a copy button for share-link.

For several lines of text, use a textarea, which this library does not have yet. When the answer comes from a short known list, use the Radio button or the Select. For a yes / no value, use the Checkbox. For a date, prefer three separate fields (day, month, year).
Layout: Label above the field
The label stays visible while typing and when the form is reviewed. The placeholder only shows an example of the format, or nothing.
Hint under the field
One short sentence on the format or the purpose of the field. In error, the hint carries the message and says how to fix it.
Width follows the answer
A postcode field is short, an email field is wider, and only free text takes the full width: the width hints at the expected format.
One column
Fields stack in a single column, 16 to 24 px apart, with related fields (an address) grouped under a legend.

Do and don’t.do: Keep a visible label above the field
Do and don’t.doText: A persistent label keeps the context while typing and when reviewing the answers.
Do and don’t.dont: Use the placeholder as the label
Do and don’t.dontText: The placeholder disappears as soon as the user types, and nothing says what the field is any more.

Do and don’t.do: Write errors that explain the fix
Do and don’t.doText: A specific message lets the user correct the value at once.
Do and don’t.dontText: A generic message says neither what is wrong nor how to fix it.

Do and don’t.do: Put essential rules in the hint
Do and don’t.doText: Rules shown before typing are read by everyone, before the first error.
Do and don’t.dont: Hide the rules behind the info icon
Do and don’t.dontText: Rules hidden in a tooltip only surface after an error, which means rework.

Do and don’t.do: Size fields to the expected answer
Do and don’t.doText: The width hints at the length and the format of the answer.
Do and don’t.dont: Stretch every field to full width
Do and don’t.dontText: Same-width fields give no cue about the expected answer.
